owner.name: Callie Munro
owner.heading: The human behind the leash
owner.bio: Callie Munro was the kid who kept a mental map of every dog on the block. After too many desk jobs and lunch breaks spent at the dog park, she finally did the obvious thing and made the dogs the job. Bluebird & Biscuit runs on routine — same walker, same route, same happy dance at the door — because dogs don't actually want variety. They want their person, their trail, and a treat at the end.

services.label: Solo walks
services.desc: One dog (or one household), one walker, zero distractions. For shy pups, seniors, and dogs who like the trail to themselves.

services.label: Pack walks
services.desc: Small matched groups of up to four. Your dog gets friends; you get a tired dog.

services.label: Drop-in visits
services.desc: A potty break, fresh water, dinner served, and fifteen minutes of undivided attention while you're stuck at work.

services.label: Overnight sitting
services.desc: We stay at your place so the routine stays theirs — same bed, same bowl, same 6 a.m. staring contest.

faq.q: Do you walk in bad weather?
faq.a: Rain, shine or Idaho sideways-snow — yes. In extreme heat or ice we shorten the route and swap in indoor play, and the visit note always says exactly what we did.

faq.q: How do you get into my house?
faq.a: Whatever you're comfortable with — a lockbox, a garage code or a smart lock. Access details live in your dog's file and nowhere else.

You know your dog's health best. For pack walks we ask that dogs stay current on whatever their vet recommends, and that you flag anything contagious before a visit. Solo walks and drop-ins are more flexible — let's talk at the meet & greet.

faq.q: How do you match pack walks?
faq.a: Slowly and on purpose. Size, energy and walking style all matter, and every new dog starts with a solo walk or two so we know who they'll love trotting next to. Max four dogs, always the same crew.
Yep — a text is enough. Pause for vacation, add a Friday, drop to twice a week. Plans bend around real life; that's the point of the week builder.

faq.q: Will I know how it went?
faq.a: Every visit ends with a photo and a quick note — where we went, what they did, anything worth flagging. You'll probably know about the squirrel before you're home.
